nodes.name: WO₃ calcination in H₂/Ar
nodes.procedure: The commercial WO₃ was placed in a tube furnace with an Ar/H₂ atmosphere, and the temperature was raised to 600 °C at a heating rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ and maintained for 120 min, and then naturally decreased to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of WO_{2.9}: The commercial WO₃ was placed in a tube furnace with an Ar/H₂ atmosphere, and the temperature was raised to 600 °C...

nodes.name: Boron modification of WO₂.₉
nodes.procedure: Disperse 50 mg of the obtained WO_{2.9} in 2 mL of deionized water (DIW) to obtain dispersion A; dissolve 500 mg of NaBH₄ in 8 mL of DIW to obtain solution B; then slowly add solution B to dispersion A to obtain a mixed solution, and mix the mixed solution. After stirring vigorously for 5 h at room temperature, the products were centrifuged and then washed five times with DIW and one time with ethanol. Finally, the catalyst was vacuum dried in a vacuum oven overnight to obtain B-WO_{2.9}.

nodes.name: Pt electrodeposition on B-WO₂.₉
nodes.procedure: Mix 5 mg of B-WO_{2.9} with 1 mL of isopropanol and 40 μL of Nafion solution, and ultrasonically disperse until uniform. Take 100 μL of the uniformly dispersed ink, and drop it on a carbon paper of 1×1 cm² five times, and clamp the paper to the working electrode after it is naturally air-dried. Electrochemical in situ deposition was conducted... in H₂-saturated 0.5 M H₂SO₄. A three-electrode system was used... Cyclic voltammetry scans were performed in the range of 0 to -0.8 V (V vs. Ag/AgCl) at a scan rate of 100 mV s⁻¹ for 20 h, until the catalyst is activated to the optimum state.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms phase transformation from WO3 (PDF#43-1035) to WO2.9 and B-WO2.9 (PDF#05-0386), with Pt/B-WO2.9 showing additional Pt nanoparticle diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the phase transformation from WO3 (PDF#43-1035) to WO2.9 and B-WO2.9 (PDF#05-0386) (Fig. 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping confirm uniform distribution of W, O, B elements and successful deposition of Pt nanoparticles on B-WO2.9 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping confirmed the uniform distribution of W, O, and B elements and successful deposition of Pt nanoparticles on the B-WO2.9 surface (Fig. 1b and Fig. S2, S3, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM, aberration corrected STEM and FFT reveal well-defined Pt crystallographic facets with Miller indices of {111} and {¯111} along the [011] direction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM), aberration corrected STEM and corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis further revealed well-defined Pt crystallographic facets with Miller indices of {111} and {¯111} along the [011] direction (Fig. 1c, d and Fig. S4, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f peaks at 71.1 eV (Pt(0) 4f7/2), 74.4 eV (Pt(0) 4f5/2), 72.3 eV (Pt(2+) 4f7/2), 75.6 eV (Pt(2+) 4f5/2); B 1s B–O peak at 192.1 eV disappears after Pt deposition; O 1s Pt–OH–W at 532.1 eV, bridge oxygen at 530.7 eV, terminal oxygen at 531.8 eV; W 4f shifts to lower BE after B treatment, higher after Pt deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was used to monitor the changes in the electronic structure of B-WO2.9 after electrodeposition. The Pt 4f spectra of Pt/B-WO2.9 show the characteristic peaks of Pt(0) 4f7/2 and Pt(0) 4f5/2 at 71.1 and 74.4 eV ... W 4f XPS spectra reveal that after B treatment, the W 4f binding energy shifts significantly to lower values.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge XANES white line peak intensity follows Pt/B-WO2.9 > WO3 > B-WO2.9 > WO2.9 valence trend.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white line (WL) peak intensity of the W L3-edge in the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra confirmed that the W valence followed the trend of Pt/B-WO2.9 > WO3 > B·WO2.9 > WO2.9 (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS at W L3-edge shows shorter W–O coordination distance in Pt/B-WO2.9 vs B-WO2.9; coordination number 1.9 for Pt/B-WO2.9; WT-EXAFS shows no Pt–W coordination, confirming Pt–O–W anchoring.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine-structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra at the W L3-edge show that the interatomic distance of the first W–O coordination shell in Pt/B-WO2.9 is slightly shorter than that in B-WO2.9 (Fig. 1f and Fig. S7, ESI†).
